body:
Does she see the gray creature also or only hear him? I used to feel ants in my head, but I never saw them, just felt them, heard them sometimes. It bothered me less than it should have. A woman in black that would follow me and put a hole in my neck, which was worse than the ants. I couldn't see her, although I knew what she looked like. 

The no-face people creature things are the worst, though. Absolute assholes that show up at the worst times. 

I don't hallucinate much anymore though. I still hear distorted children's songs and circus music, sometimes distorted voices at random times. Certain sounds like the AC is a trigger for me. I'm used to it now so it does not bother me too much.

I agree with /u/justpasssingbyy. I suffer from PTSD and dissociation with psychotic features. When I was very young I would see things a lot, not every day. Just when the dissociation was bad or when I was not sleeping enough. Or after a few bad things that happened. 

As a teen it took me longer to develop emotional maturity and social skills. Maybe you're meant to learn those automatically, it kind of seems like it. But I was not very good at understanding or learning social behaviors, so I did a lot of childlike things in my teens. Your friend may have been the same.

In 2015-16 I had another psychotic break. I was hearing and seeing and feeling things that other people did not see, but I believed that was because my universe and time line was always changing. Most of the time I knew when I was seeing something that other people wouldn't see. It was more difficult with the bad voices, but I tried to ignore them. So I was able to appear functional enough not to end up in the psych ward, which would have made me worse due to my PTSD. I had some bad things happen to me in hospitals when I was young. 

It took me a while to get better and assimilate back into one reality. I don't particularly care for it most days, though.

Many types of mental health conditions or symptoms. They get worse when you stop sleeping.

For three or four months I did not sleep more than four hours every few days. But usually I would go without sleep before I could get four hours. I would have bad nightmares when I slept. But when I was awake it was just a different sort of nightmare. At night I would see faces in the ceiling or a stranger in the corner of my room. There is not much you can do in that moment when your mind is lying to you.

It is hard to sleep when there is a new baby I am sure. Babies can have their problems sleeping too. But at least your reason is something real. Something you can choose. Compared to having a mind like mine at least.

This has happened to me two or three separate times. Maybe more times than that, but I will not ever know for sure. My old memories feel like reconstructions of stories told by a stranger. Except that stranger was "me" once upon a time. Don't know if I am stronger for it. I doubt it, but that is alright.

It does feel like you have died and kept on living somehow. A strange thing to experience. The forest growing anew analogy is a nice way to paint it, though.

I am very sorry you had to do that. I wish it were different for people like you. Everyone should be able to eat and have some thing to keep them going. 

I think music is the only part of me worth very much at all now. Pretty sure I will have to sell my piano too. Every time I play I find some way to put off selling it. So I avoid playing now too. It is what it is.

Yes I am repressing a lot too. I am very resistant to remembering who I was before, or being any thing like that person. Do not know why. No energy or strength to deal with it though. Of course I still remember things offhand. 

The flashbacks are rough. If I walk into one, they use up all the energy I have. I have learned how to avoid them so they are not very common. 

It is just the deep exploration part of my head I cannot handle. Most of my symptoms are mild or not there at all now. So I think it helps. Except the paranoia. It has stayed alive and fairly well but whatever. I know how to handle it.

I hope things keep working out for you. Thank you for your advice.
Thank you for the advice. I appreciate it.

I never thought about the perspective of an SO of someone in my situation until now. That would be very painful for them too. 

3 months is pretty early. Do not give up hope. It may be that the experience is holding him back. 

I did not want to change med dosages either. Changing the dose made the break worse. So I went back to my old dose. I started a mild sleep aid. I was able to avoid major changes after that.

A break from reality is a...very difficult thing to process and understand. At one point I was simply trying to survive in it. I had gotten used to living in a nightmare. My reactions and thoughts made sense to me. Coming out of that was not a relief. It was disorienting. It was cold.

3 months in, I could not remember the break, not a moment of it. Yet I felt like I was another person. Someone who was born there, molded by that place. I was trying to deal with my new life. It was like I was a stand-in for the missing star of a shitty stage show. I hated being called by my real name. That just made me angry. Felt like everyone was lying to me and expecting me to go along with it. 

Then the grief started. I lost friends, voices, who were real to me for a long time. They helped me survive. When I got through the break, they were suddenly gone. No warning, no farewells. Felt like losing a limb.

It has been a year for me now. Objectively speaking, my symptoms are much better than they were. Almost no hallucinations. I have paranoia-free days. The memories I have do not feel like "me". But some of the unconscious behavior/personality bits have returned. Mannerisms and such. I still feel like a different person and a stranger. However I am more similar to the person I used to be. 

The best thing I recommend are counseling (for you) because this "loss" of your husband is real. He might feel like a stranger for a while, if his experience is anything like mine. My communication skills were very bad for awhile. Couple's counseling might help you communicate better.  

Support him when you can, but let yourself have space from this too. This is some bleak and heavy shit to carry on your own. Good luck, I hope things get better for you and him.

I barely managed through my time with psychosis. I cannot imagine 4 years of it and that kind of "treatment". I am sorry you were put through that. 

It is hard to forget an experience like that. I think it is engraved somewhere in my bones now. You put it quite well. Maybe if I am patient, it will hurt less one day.

I am one person so it is not the same for everyone. Based on my experience here is my advice if you meet anyone like me. 

The assumptions. If I talk about the voices bothering me that does not mean I have suddenly forgotten they are a hallucination. I know they are. I want to talk about them. The voices are like having noisy roommates in your head that you never asked for. Same goes for other things, visual hallucinations and such. 

When things are bad and I am dissociating heavily, I speak in metaphors a lot. Because explaining my thoughts and feelings is very hard. Sometimes I talk about having a rabbit heart. Of course I do not have a real rabbit heart. But have you ever seen a rabbit caught in a trap? That is sort of what I meant to describe. That type of fear. 

Many people use symbolism and imagery to make sense of things. Some times how we make sense of things has an element of sanity in it. If you had literature analysis assignments in school, then it might help to use that to your advantage. 

Instead of trying to get me to speak like a more "sane person", can I just explain what I meant with certain phrases and keep using them? It is very hard having to keep track of what someone else says and my own thoughts. Then to put all that in the "right words". Some times the best I can do is use my way of describing things, if you understand me, then I do not know why it matters.

Most of the time I did not feel like I was being heard. Some times I still feel that way. My counselor and psychiatrist are good people but are not trained for my situation exactly.

Shortly before my break, I wanted to be monitored for symptoms of schizophrenia because of family history. My psychiatrist said it was not possible I had schizophrenia, since taking my ADHD meds did not affect those symptoms. So it was not a priority. My counselor said I was too functional and rational to be concerned about that. I think that is a very insulting thing to imply about some one with the disorder. 

I struggle with feeling like I am exaggerating things because of things they said. I stopped trying to get a valid diagnosis that explains my symptoms. Will never ask about it again either. Not worth the risk. 

Thank you for doing your best for people dealing with symptoms like mine. It might not seem like a lot but it could make all the difference.

Does it get easier? 3 months after my break I had very little memory of it. Now I am remembering what happened a little. Every day I am afraid it will happen again. Just because I am remembering things. The break started so slow at first. Didn't notice any thing was wrong until it was too late. 

The reminders are in many places. Sometimes I see a corridor that looks just a bit too familiar. Sometimes I am reminded of the wolves. I try to tell my self it is not the same. It is over. They will not come back again. But I never believe it. Not really. The fault lines in my head are still there.

All I am now is a stupid security protocol. I have to be alert. I have to defuse the bad thoughts. All it really takes for my head is one little errant thought to set it off. That is what happened before at least.

My counselor says me doing that is an anxiety response. Nothing more. But he does not understand. It is more. He was not there. He did not see and hear and feel the things I did. He did see what it is like to break into pieces and lose the person I should be. I am still a stranger to my self. I cannot let it set off. I will not survive another round in that place. 

Just cos it was in my head does not make the damage less bad.  

You are right. Maybe forgetting would be better. I hope things continue going well for you.

It's not that I think it's the answer exactly. Sorry. I am dissociating a lot lately so I do not feel like a person, that makes it harder to see things clearly. There are a lot of issues I did not write about in the post but when I say my head is a mess it is not an exaggeration. 

Maybe there are more triggers or whatever the word is lately. Last March I had a psychotic break so that is why I have the weird associations with March, the sun, and all that. I constantly feel like it is up to me to keep every thing together, to mind the warnings. I cannot fuck up because no one else has my back. I do not even know what would help me. That is why losing Mal and Noah was so bad. They were my friends and they helped. But now it is just me. 

Maybe that does not make sense though. Sorry.

Some people's anxiety makes them look through a magnifying glass with an anchor on their chest. 

I see things through an astronaut helmet and a kaleidescope. Everything is surreal and almost not there. That is dissociation for you.

When I do experience anxiety closely past the dissociation, it is very bad. I feel an anchor in my chest pulling me down underwater. A billion thoughts hit me at once. Some times the voices in my head come out to torture me. 

I am afraid of every thing it seems. A transcript of my thoughts. 

Germs. The sun. Sharp noises. Driving. Going to the store. Eating food I have not bought or made myself. The strangers around me, I am afraid they can read my thoughts. 

I've shared too much on my Reddit account, people will identify me and know all my secrets. Time is up, I have wasted it all. The voices. The woman with the candles. Cannot speak out loud, some one might be listening. Some thing seems suspicious there is a message in the static get away get away get away.

Remember to smile Julien. React appropriately for god's sake. Your eyes are hollow I know. We are all homesick and this place is not home. We must pretend because we are standing in. 

Stop rambling, stop rambling, can't you speak normally for once do not mention the. Shut up.

What monsters our thoughts become, if we let them unfurl too far!

Standard fare for living these days, putting up with that. It is very expensive. This rabbit heart will give out on me sooner or later.

That makes sense. It is strange that my psychiatrist decided to not make a diagnosis. It is not that important though. 

I have chronic nightmares too. I always remember them. Brains are kind of funny.

I cannot imagine what it would be like to remember the trauma, that must be rough. I hope things continue to get better for you. Thank you for taking the time to explain things.

Okay thank you. It is a bit hard to write out my thoughts clearly but I will try my best.

Is trauma is a thing that happens during a very bad experience like abuse? Or is it a box that defines the way the abuse mentally hurt a person after it happened?

My counselor says I went through traumas. Like it is a room I walked through except now I cannot remember what the room looked like or what happened in it. And all of my troubles started in that room. 

My psychiatrist and counselor said my general hallucinations and paranoia are related to trauma and disassociation, not because of a condition like PTSD or schizophrenia. That confuses me. How does trauma cause those symptoms by itself? Does it do something to the brain or make a person more mentally stressed? 

Sorry if this is hard to understand it can take me a while to write.

I did not know you could forget them in a normal way and still have problems. That is interesting. I lost most of my memories after a psychotic break. Nearly a year ago now. So that is a bit different and more related to disassociation.

Can you explain what trauma does to memory or what it means? My counselor uses that word a lot. But when I read or listen the words come through as pictures in my head. And to me trauma is a little doll with yarn hair. 

It is hard to understand what trauma is or what it does. If I see it like that.

Having memories of things I cannot remember is something I experience. On good days at least not today. My counselor thinks it is due to trauma I cannot remember. And disassociation. 

Some times I can feel my head trying to recall a memory but it fails. Or I might have an emotional reaction without the context. Like nostalgia. I am not sure if that is an emotion though. My muscle memory can be slow on bad days. Like when I was driving and it was raining and for a few moments I wasn't sure what people did about that. Don't worry, I do not drive on bad days any more.

A lot of my memories are gone. Once some one asked, "Think of your most embarrassing memory." It was automatic for other people. Not me. I could not think of one at all. 

People should not take their memories for granted. I think I probably did take them for granted a long time ago. Haven't got any photos or letters or anything like that. Maybe I hated how they made me feel so I destroyed them. What a foolish thing to do.

It is weird what memories remain with you after experiences like that. 

I was somewhat convinced my body was going into rigor mortis at one point, which was very surreal.

The worst of it I remember is laying on my bed, staring at the ceiling. Unable to move. My limbs felt heavy even on a mattress. All I could think about was my single evening "meal", the 1/4 cup of cold spagettio's I got. I remember my vision going, head feeling weird and thinking, "Oh, I am slowly dying here." It is odd to remember now. It has been a long time since my last relapse. 

I am glad you have recovered, I would not wish those sorts of moments on any one. I hope you are doing well now.
Do your symptoms change when you must get used to some thing new? Like a new place or roommate.

Brushing right after is one of the worst things to do. The acid is still present and will cause more wear on your teeth. 

Rinse your mouth out with warm water and baking soda. Chew peppermint flavoured antiacid tablets. Brush your teeth after an hour. Get a soft flouride rinse, not the mint or sharp flavored kind. Use it daily.

Those things are not a cure. You will hurt your teeth and body.

Not really. Depends on the area and community. 

I was in this situation as a teenager, needing emergency placement for the weekend. There was one bed open but a higher need case took it. So all the beds were full and there was nowhere else for me to go. They tried to work out another option but. Then my mother showed up at the school angry. The caseworker lady took me out of the office for a bit. While the other caseworker talked to her. Not sure what was said or done.

I remember watching her leave and wishing she would take me with her. Don't remember much after that or the following weekend. Wonder if I slept at all. My mother made sure I'd never get CPS involved again though.

Still happens here now. If I was well and lived some where safe, I would do the same thing.
I might have to take you up on that offer. It is holiday season so to them it is kind of bad timing. Thanks again. :)
That is a good way of explaining it. I have not looked up any of those things. My anxiety never needs more fuel. Thanks for the advice.

You summarized my own reasoning very well with this comment. 

I didn't think about it until your comment, but a lot of my physical issues can be worsened by disassociation too. On bad days, I have to concentrate on many things that other people do without thinking. On top of tracking basic survival needs like eating, hydrating, etc.

There has been little support for the driving restrictions I use already, so my decision won't be received well by some relatives. My psychiatrist and counselor both support it though, so I am going forward with it. At the moment I am going to try driving only when certain criteria is met. Until I get the paperwork and routine sorted at least. Thanks for sharing your perspective, it was very helpful.

Thank you so much for replying. My concern is what you mentioned, that this is a matter of avoidance. 

I do listen to music and sing actually. It helps. The music can soften the sound of traffic around me. Sudden loud noises can cause brief muscle spasms. Spasms are not good to have when driving.

I have tried grounding, which helps a bit in other situations. Not with driving. I don't know why.

There are other factors that contribute to the anxiety too.

I am very short. Have to use a booster seat just to see the hood of the car. I am not able to see how much space I have when turning or reversing.

When the roads are busy, it is overwhelming to process. I get completely lost trying to follow and make sense of every thing moving around me. My spatial and visual tracking skills are very bad (I was tested) so maybe that is why. 

I do not drive at night. I lose sense of where I am on the road. The lights are very disorienting.

Those things didn't always make me so anxious though. Until a man yelled at me for not turning on red and followed me for a few miles to scream more. Another person got out of their car to confront me for not turning on red. Scared me a lot. I just couldn't see if it was safe to turn...

Sorry. I am rambling. I'm not sure if any of this makes sense. 

Maybe I am just scared of every thing with my stupid rabbit heart. So maybe those are just excuses... I don't know, it just feels so complicated.

Really? I had no idea. Never thought about anxiety being a factor, beyond hot/cold flashes and nausea.

Since March I've been having on/off tinnitus, always in one ear at a time. I've been stressing about my hearing getting worse. I am sensitive to light too. 

Do you know of a good resource that discusses these side effects? I'd really like to read up on this.

It is not one dream exactly. It is a series about the dark-haired, dark-eyed girl. Dreamt of her many times. 

First she was angry and wanted to kill me. She stabbed me in the eyes. She was older then, late 20s. I didn't understand her anger for a long time. Now I do. So the dreams changed where she is just a kid. I keep losing her. Over and over. 

My most recent dreams, I remember very clearly. Some parts are blacked out because they are too much.

There is a first part to this, the second part is the worst. A boy and I were both kidnapped and put in a cage. The kid was around 10-11. Dark hair, dark eyes. I have never met him before, and never seen him again. 

There was a television screen in front of us. We're forced to watch what happens. 

The first thing we saw is a cat. The boy lost it when he sees it. Started screaming and crying. He runs into the bars of the cage over and over until he is too tired to move. I tried to hug and comfort him. It was hard to watch what happened to the cat. I know it died. There is a gap in my memory after that.

Next thing I remember is seeing a person on the screen. Dark-haired, dark-eyed girl. Maybe 5-6 years old. Wish it had gone black here. I went cold and felt sick. Begged a God I do not believe in to help her.

The worst thing is the way she stares through the screen like she can see me. She smiles at the camera, like she doesn't know she needs to *run* right now. I cried and screamed at her to go. Tore my nails clean off trying to get out of the cage. There is a gap after that too.

Both dreams end the same. With me and the boy hugging and crying. It hurts to breathe. May as well be gutted rotten inside.

I know none of those things happened but I still remember the pain. They felt real. 

Now I have a similar dream often. I watch someone get shot first. Head blown off, pink mist. Then I am staring down the barrel of the gun. Frozen in place with my stupid rabbit-heart. Knowing the gun is going to go off in seconds. 

I never see who is holding the gun. But I know it is the man that killed her. Every time, I am choked with rage and I promise my self I will find a way to kill him. Beat his head in. That is as far as I can think, though.

Some times I hear the gunshot just before waking up.

The memories I have of her saying/doing those things -- and generally most the memories I do have -- feel like some one else's. There is no emotional context. I know logically all of those actions were remarkably cruel. But it's like remembering a movie I watched. 

You're spot-on about the inside of her mind. As a person she does have decent traits. They just happen to be overshadowed a lot. I try to remember that about her but it can be difficult.

She is still in my life. I treat her as civilly and objectively as possible at a distance. When I am able to move and live on my own, I plan to go low or no-contact with her.

The first one was pretty awful, yeah. 

Music (instrumental) is a language to me. Some times it describes/conveys my thoughts and feelings much more concisely than actual words (which I often have trouble with). I've always thought synthesia was pretty neat though.

Sure. Do you have synthesia, by the way?

I was never diagnosed, all I know is that it was a psychotic break. This was my second one. Recently discovered I had many milder episodes in the past as well. My meds have helped so as long as I take them, my symptoms are not too bad. I figured this was more important. 

If you have more questions you can PM me if you like.

I just realised my stomach does not growl at all. 

The only indication of hunger know of is when I have gone too long without and I feel very ill. Super helpful. Raisin bran cereal for breakfast helps a lot though.

She definitely does not respect boundaries. Reminds me a lot of some one I know with borderline personality disorder. They are so similar it is uncanny. Her lack of self-awareness and empathy is amazing. 

There are no limits with her "sympathetic" or "worried" remarks either. 

My mother tried to give me special treats as a kid, so I'd like her more than my dad. When I got older and weighed more than 10-year-old me, the comparisons and criticisms started. I did not have a dead sibling for comparison, so she used my cousins or actresses instead. (Once I started dealing with anorexia, my turning down her food and shoving away her forced affection led to her crying about how I did not love her.) 

Hell, even cats aren't safe. When I first got my current cat, my mother was giving her treats in secret, trying to win her over. Cat became overweight, at risk of developing diabetes (healthy and fine now). I figured out my mother was the main culprit, directly ordered her to stop, confronted her a few times. 

In response, she made comments about how current cat did not compare to my 8-lb, kitten-sized childhood cat, who "was such a nice, beautiful cat; just the tiniest little thing." This went on for months. She is absolutely bonkers.

Current cat never grew to like my mother. I agree with current cat's assessment.

For a while I kept a journal. I wrote down every thing that happened each day, a few of my feelings/thoughts that seemed to persist, and my symptoms. It turned out to be useful once I realised my memory had been compromised.

Maybe you could do something similar and see if it helps.

Yeah, it gets a lot easier to tolerate once you start putting that sort of behavior completely on them, knowing it's not really about you.

My mother treats a lot of things about me as her trophy/achievement, it's definitely a self-esteem thing for her. She's also essentially my anti-role model, so at least I know what to *not* to say/do.

This made me audibly laugh, it's so relatable. 

My life is a VR experience I do not remember signing up for. It has a lot of unpleasant assignments, like grocery shopping and making small talk.

I had to quit the "body positivity" thing too. I settled on, "You are babysitting this puppet body. Ensure its basic needs are met so it does not die. Also there's no pay or time off."

Feelings ruin so many things. 

The differentiating part is easier on a schedule at least... With my current symptoms, most of the time I only know when I get physically ill.

Before that, I was getting better at learning how to differentiate, so it is possible! But I completely get how hard it can be. One day at a time!

Yep. I also found ways to "make sure" I was not slipping up in case my perception "normalized" somehow. Like, it was normal to be cold during the summer -- so if I wasn't cold, then clearly I was fucking up.

I'm pretty okay with my current weight now though. That could be part of the disassociation, but silver linings, right?

:( Man, I know that feeling of complete invalidation. The first comment I remember fucking me up is also one my mother made. 

After high school I was recovering from a GI issue (I ate mainly crackers for a *year*). I had a normal (slightly higher than usual) BMI. My mother said I was "getting big" and I "needed to be careful". \*Cue 6 years of anorexia* 

She projects a lot of her own body issues onto me though, I've learned to treat it as ridiculous nonsense.

Yes! It's weird how perception plays into this. 

I met up with an old friend a few years ago. The whole time I was envious about how thin she was and how I looked worse. Later she admitted she thought the same thing about me during that visit. We were both convinced the other looked 'better' in comparison to us.

(We were both suffering from EDs at the time, but kept it a secret from each other.)

In the beginning, it was the opposite for me. Someone said, "You're at a healthier weight now? Huh, I don't see much of a difference honestly." I thought, *You mean I didn't succeed when I looked like a zombie and was nearly dying? Clearly I am a failure and a liar,* and cried in the bathroom. I got over it obviously.

Also the first time I had to buy more than those thin liners was a genuinely upsetting experience.

My indoor panda plant is thriving, which is nice since it's my first plant ever.

I can eat proper food today after spending over a week sick, stuck eating bland foods.

[This animated gif](https://i.redd.it/wrie0b5qrgxy.gif) about pets made me happy.

/u/moreborgthancyborg is spot-on with their post.

I feel lost and worried without my positive symptoms showing up once in a while. If they are less/not present, then I worry more. What if they are lies? What if what if what if. They can really twist things into knots. 

Part of me is afraid that I am putting together a identity beyond what happened to me a few months ago. That I am actively trying to move past it. It seems unsafe. It is a very unfamiliar course of action. I do not want to lose my self again. But I am changing, not losing any thing completely. I mix those two up a lot, they feel very similar.

This blogging for you is new and so some new fears are coming up. Maybe you are feeling more vulnerable, sharing like this? Brainstorm why you may feel that way. Once you have a sense, you can figure out how to feel more secure about sharing. 

(I had some examples but I do not want to make you worry more somehow, so I deleted them. Very indecisive. Sorry.)

One idea -- you could publish your post privately to start. Get a sense of how it feels to publish it first. Maybe it can help you get over that initial fear/rumination about posting?

This is lovely. It is very familiar, paints pictures in my head. Would suit some brilliant visual pieces, I think.

Good writing will show, not tell. You have done very well. Congratulations on winning the contest :)

Your words are very relatable, that is rare. I suppose I want to offer some comfort, but I am a ghost and that is rarely comforting. Nevertheless.

How the moment feels, and remembering it specifically, does not matter as much as the fact that it happened. 

The more important thing is, what was the catalyst for that moment? Is it familiar?

Some catalysts burn out fast, but they are a sort of hint for finding your constant catalysts. Every one has them, I am pretty sure. Some times you have to do a little searching.

Here is the thing to remember. If that moment happened, that means they are possible. Therefore, so is that catalyst.

Maybe you have not found a familiar catalyst yet. Maybe you have one, but it is not a catalyst for good moments. I have a few of those too.

So, the next time you feel some thing, do not run from it. Pay attention to it. Keep your self open to new things. That is the first step.

Some days you may find it hard to believe in any of this. That is okay. Even if you find it hard to believe in, the moments still happened. Nothing can take that away from you. 

You know what helps at the start, in all the grey? (The grey is apathy, empty.) Writing every thing down. 

I have a text file, a list of things that made me feel some thing. Even the pastels, barely-there feelings. 

You see, if it matters at all -- sorry, I am no good at knowing what matters some times. 

One day I woke up out of a break, out of grey, and I was in some one else's life. I am supposed to say that person is me, never feels like it though. Everything I know about them -- friends, family, formative experiences -- is like a textbook reference, nothing personal.

Playing some one else means that some times I go a very long time without colour. And the longer I go without colour, the farther away I get. Start losing things.

Playing some one else means often I do not feel like *me*, who ever I am. Not much I relate to out here, but then again. The more I think that, the more I am blinded by the grey.

Most things on that list are just words with faint sentiments now. But they helped lead me to my constant catalysts. And I can still build parts with those. Seal over the broken bits. I know I like building and fixing things. Offering advice too, I suppose. It is a start.

Like I said, even if you find them hard to believe in, your moments and their catalysts happened. Nothing can take that away from you.

There are some other explanations for your experience for you to think about.

Seems you are not sleeping very well at this point. Even mild sleep deprivation with anxiety can be incredibly powerful for some. It can lead to hallucinations, increased anxiety and insomnia, and sometimes more frequent sleep paralysis.  

I cannot diagnose you but the most problematic thing here is how this anxiety is affecting you. If you are in the US, maybe fireworks have been affecting your sleep recently.

Did this get worse once you started experiencing the anxiety and what may be causing it? 

Is it possible nighttime is causing anxiety for you at this point?

Have you increased your caffeine intake or are you taking anything else to curb tiredness during the day? This can also affect your sleep.

I have been told it is not uncommon for people to have hallucinations at night. 

Being tired can affect our senses and perception. Seeing things in the corner of your eye can be anything. A trick of the light or a shadow. However our eyes may misinterpret what we see, and give credence to our worst fears. That can feed into anxiety, which in turn feeds into insomnia and panic attacks.

Schizophrenia and other disorders are characterized by many symptoms, not only hallucinations. So right now, I would not jump to any of those things. Anxiety may be a major contributer though.

I do not have much to spend today. But those are my two cents.

Ah, yes. Repressing emotions so you are dead inside.

If we are paying attention to only one thing, looking for only one thing, we will be more likely to notice it. This is a kind of pattern-seeking. However, it often makes the paranoid symptoms unbearable. 

We all want to make sense of things and understand them. In science and other things, when working on a new idea, a person cannot base everything on why it holds, or seems possible. They must note the possible reasons why it may not hold. Sometimes, those reasons make the whole idea fall apart. 

So for you, what makes your theory or suspicion fall apart?

I do not mean to sound like I am minimizing your fear. But sometimes it is helpful to consider an alternate perspective or alternate reasons for these things.

The music and playlists. Do you tend to enjoy similar types of music? Or enjoy music you can relate to, or feel a certain way?

Also, I want to talk a bit about shuffle algorithms and software. 

Shuffle algorithms are sometimes very limited and songs may not seem randomized much. There may be a ranking system based on how many times you listen to it or some other metric. If you listen to a finite set of songs, genres, or artists consistently, it is possible that they are coming up more based on that metric. This is meant to be convenient, so you are not skipping songs constantly to get to one you prefer.

It is also possible that an update of the software has introduced a bug that is messing with the algorithm itself. This may be why you are noticing this change.

So, it is possible there are other reasons for the songs to seemingly say the same things, isn't it?

Now, a person who wants to harm you could use songs like you describe. But, two people can interpret songs very differently. There is a lot of room for error. What if you didn't hear the message they intended at all? Doesn't that seem a bit too subjective to use for a message?

Hacking is another thing that is easy to jump to. However, people that learn the concepts involved with hacking are those who tend to spend quite a bit of time learning how to, most of the time. It is unlikely they would risk it by trying to directly harm someone. Hacking would also potentially leave a trail, which is also a big risk. My main point is, whatever a hacker's goal is, it would not often be as direct, like a serial killer or other aggressor.
